Airbnb: Consistent Yearly Growth and Major Seasonal Spikes

Airbnb (NASDAQ:ABNB) primarily generates its revenue by managing a global digital marketplace that connects individual property hosts offering private rooms, primary residences, and vacation homes with travelers seeking unique lodging experiences, custom local activities, and tailored vacation rentals worldwide.

It recently entered an exclusive property booking partnership integrating over one million listings into the American Express platform, and it formally introduced updated operational policies restricting hosts from assigning specific professional checkout chores to visiting guests.

Booking: Higher Overall Scale Meets Recent Revenue Decline

Booking (NASDAQ:BKNG) functions as a global provider of digital travel and dining reservations, earning revenue through a diverse portfolio of consumer platforms that offer extensive accommodation bookings, airline tickets, rental cars, vacation packages, cruise itineraries, and online restaurant reservations across international markets.

It recently introduced a new artificial intelligence-powered personal travel agent tool to enhance consumer booking experiences, while simultaneously navigating a Federal Trade Commission investigation regarding specific marketing and billing practices at its Priceline brand.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue here refers to the data provider's standardized income-statement revenue line item, which serves as a fundamental financial tracking metric that shows individual investors exactly how much total money a business brings in from its core operations before any administrative, marketing, payroll, or operational expenses are deducted by the company's management.

Airbnb (ABNB) stock returned 53.6% in the year to November 16, 2026, against 11.4% for the S&P 500. Investors who held the shares through that run may wonder whether the easy money is gone, while those on the sidelines might ask if they are too late. So if you bought Airbnb today and held it for three years, what could the shares return, and what would have to go right?

What Would Three Years Of Holding Airbnb Return?

Based on our assumptions, holding Airbnb for three years would return about 21.9% on the share price alone. Three variables shape that figure: how fast revenue grows, the operating margin Airbnb earns on it, and the P/E the market pays for those earnings. Revenue growth drives all of that gain and more. The scenario assumes revenue grows 14.2% a year, representing 85% of the pace Airbnb reported for the twelve months to September 2026. A slightly lower margin and a lower P/E in year three both subtract from the overall return.

Airbnb's Growth Is Picking Up Again

Management said on the November 5 call that revenue grew 19% in fiscal Q3 2026, marking the fastest pace in more than three years. The company's guide for fiscal Q4 2026 calls for revenue growth of 16% to 18%, which includes about 2 points from currency. That single quarter's pace sits above the scenario's yearly rate.

Guests are also booking more. Nights and seats booked rose 16% from a year earlier, though management said about 3 points of that increase came from Reserve Now, Pay Later, a feature that lets guests book without paying up front.

The company is adding newer ways to sell stays as well. Hotels on Airbnb are growing markedly faster than the core business, management said, and in October the company launched an exclusive partnership with American Express that brings Airbnb listings to Amex Travel.

Jim Cramer and Cathie Wood are two of the most closely followed voices on Wall Street, and we regularly cover the stocks they like. Once a Wall Street darling, Cathie Wood has struggled to replicate her success from the pandemic days as shifting market dynamics have weighed on her disruptive innovation bets. You can see her latest 13F filing here.

Wood's flagship ARK Innovation ETF (BATS:ARKK) is down about 4% so far this year, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up about 10%. ARKK had gained about 16% through the end of September, and a sharp tech selloff in October and early November erased that gain and pushed the fund below where it started the year.  As of Nov. 12, her Ark Innovation ETF has delivered a five-year annualized return of -8.23%, while the S&P 500 has an annualized return of 10.15% over the same period, according to data from Morningstar.

In August, ARK kept buying Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) across five funds while investors worried about an AI bubble, and it sold some Roblox shares. Check out the full story here.

Wood addressed the selloff in her latest In The Know episode on YouTube, and she thinks the market overreacted to the midterm elections. She said stocks have usually risen in the year after a midterm election, by roughly 13% to 14% in the periods she showed. She also tried to calm fears that data center projects will slow down. Wood said data centers in communities like those in Virginia have lowered property taxes and paid for new schools, and she blamed the negative headlines for hiding that. She also thinks AI spending is still at an early stage.

Wood expects AI to lift productivity, keep inflation lower than most investors expect, and push US real GDP growth to 7%. Cramer has also talked about the data center backlash. He said AI executives now face criticism over rising electricity bills, resource use and job losses, and he still likes certain AI stocks. Click to see the stocks he still likes.

Methodology

To compile this list, we reviewed ARK Investment Management's third-quarter 2026 portfolio, as disclosed in its latest 13F filing, and identified stocks that Jim Cramer has spoken positively about in his recent CNBC commentary. We prioritized well-known companies and excluded stocks in which ARK reduced its shareholdings by more than 5% during the quarter. We then ranked the 10 selected stocks in ascending order of the number of hedge funds holding stakes in them at the end of the second quarter of 2026, using Insider Monkey's database of 1,006 hedge funds. ARK's holdings and changes reflect the third quarter, while the hedge fund ownership figures reflect the second quarter. To see where ARK stood going into the year, check our list Cathie Wood 2026 Portfolio: 10 Best Stocks to Buy. For more of Cramer's recent favorites, see Jim Cramer Is Bullish on These 10 Stocks Amid Nvidia (NVDA) Controversy.

title: Is There Still A Reason To Own Expedia Stock?

Is There Still A Reason To Own Expedia Stock?

Today's big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash

Expedia (EXPE) stock fell 4.8% over the past year, while the S&P 500 returned 11.4%. The company continued to repurchase its own shares anyway. In the four quarters to September 2026, Expedia spent an amount equal to 5.3% of its current market value on buybacks, net of stock paid to employees. So how much more does each Expedia share earn because of the buybacks?

How Much More Each Expedia Share Now Earns

Over the past three years, Expedia's earnings per share grew 45.4% a year, against 35.8% a year for its net income. That is a gap of 9.7 percentage points a year. Each share earned more than profit growth alone would give it because there were fewer shares to split that profit among: the diluted share count fell from 148 million in the twelve months to September 2023 to 122 million in the twelve months to September 2026.

The number of shares you hold remains the same. Each one simply claims a larger slice of Expedia's earnings, though the market value of that slice still depends on the share price.

Expedia Pays For Its Buybacks Out Of Cash Flow

Expedia covers the buybacks with cash generated by its travel business, which continues to expand. Revenue in the business-to-business (B2B) segment grew 18.0% in fiscal 2025, compared with 2.2% for the business-to-customer side, which is still the larger of the two.

In the twelve months to September 30, 2026, Expedia generated free cash flow equal to 1.6 times the $2.28 billion it distributed through buybacks and dividends. During a November 4, 2026 call, management said this cash has fueled the return of capital to shareholders.

Expedia also reduced its debt burden while repurchasing shares. Total debt fell to $5.69 billion at September 30, 2026, down from $6.48 billion a year earlier. Cash and short-term investments of $5.57 billion nearly match that debt. Over the past twelve months, operating income covered interest expense 8.4 times.

Why Expedia's Expected Slowdown Matters To Shareholders

Profit growth, rather than a smaller share count, drove most of the earnings increase for each Expedia share. Because of this, a business slowdown would show up in what each share earns.

Management expects the business to slow in fiscal Q4 2026, guiding for revenue growth of 4% to 5.7%, compared with the 11.9% reported for fiscal Q3 2026. Management pointed to the timing of its fall sale, which pulled demand into the third quarter, and cited a softer environment that includes the U.S. election cycle and travel disruptions across EMEA. The company still raised its full-year forecast after the third quarter came in above the high end of its own guidance.

title: What Would Unrest In Europe Do To Airbnb Stock?

What Would Unrest In Europe Do To Airbnb Stock?

If you own Airbnb (ABNB), the worry is simple: that travelers book fewer trips on Airbnb because of unrest in France and the conflict in the Middle East. Management named both on its November 5, 2026 call and said it is closely monitoring developments in Europe. Its forecast for the October-to-December quarter assumes no material lasting impact from either. So what did Airbnb's latest quarter show, and what would reveal damage ahead?

Airbnb Grew Faster In France In Fiscal Q3 2026

Airbnb's growth accelerated across all five of its core markets during the July-to-September quarter, including France and the U.K., management said on the November 5 call. Management put Airbnb's growth across Europe, the Middle East and Africa in the mid-teens, and said all four of its regions grew faster than they did in the April-to-June quarter.

That same day, Airbnb raised its full-year outlook to revenue growth in the high teens, up from mid-teens, as demand picked up across its global markets. The worry therefore centers on the months ahead rather than the period just reported, and management is watching the same regions you are.

Most Of Airbnb's Profit Comes From July To September

A year earlier, the October-to-December quarter produced $269 million in operating income, compared to $2.02 billion during the July-to-September quarter just reported. Those July-to-September months generated most of the $3.13 billion in operating income Airbnb earned over the past twelve months.

So how long any unrest lasts matters for Airbnb. Unrest that faded by the end of 2026 would land on one of Airbnb's lighter quarters for profit, while unrest that lasted into July-to-September 2027 would reach far more of it. For the nearer quarter, management forecasts revenue of $3.22 billion to $3.28 billion, up 16% to 18% from a year earlier.

Airbnb Holds Net Cash, Yet Its Stock Fell Harder In Past Shocks

At the end of September, Airbnb held $12.6 billion in cash and short-term investments, against $2.41 billion of debt. Management said the company generated $4.9 billion of free cash flow over the past twelve months. Those figures make a few weak quarters a question about Airbnb's growth rather than its finances.

The share price has been less steady than the business. Airbnb stock fell 33% in the 2025 tariff shock, against 19% for the SPY fund that tracks the S&P 500. In the 2022 inflation shock and Fed tightening, it fell 48%, against 24% for the same fund. Over the past year to November 13, 2026, Airbnb stock returned 53.5%, against 11.7% for the S&P 500.

title: What Airbnb Holders Bought Into
detail:
What Airbnb Holders Bought Into
Bailey Pemberton
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:11 AM CST 4 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

If you only skimmed the 2025 debate on Airbnb, with bulls calling it a lifestyle platform in the making and bears warning of regulatory walls and slowing core markets, you might not have expected the outcome. Holding Airbnb over the past year would have returned 49.5%, including dividends. If you had faced that split view back in November 2025, what in the record could have justified taking the risk anyway?

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

The easy part of this move is behind Airbnb. Zero in on 32 high quality undervalued stocks for companies trading below our estimates.

The Two Airbnb Stories Investors Were Choosing Between

The shares cost US$123 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Airbnb then had to pick between two very different but reasonable stories about what that price implied.

On the bullish side, the July 2025 Narrative from User argued Airbnb could justify a Fair Value of US$164, built on revenue growth of 12.0% and a 25.0% profit margin as it pushed further into lifestyle use cases and international markets.

The May 2025 bearish case pointed to a Fair Value of US$96, stressing regulatory pressure, housing affordability criticism, and the risk that tighter rules and compliance costs would restrict listings and squeeze profitability.

NasdaqGS:ABNB 1-Year Stock Price Chart
What The Airbnb Evidence Actually Tested

Airbnb's Q3 2026 report showed revenue at US$4.9b and net income at US$1.9b, with net margin moving from 33.6% in Q3 2025 to 38.8%. That combination supported the bullish Narrative that assumed strong profitability on a larger platform. Regulatory friction still appeared through actions such as Chicago's lawsuit, so the period's evidence pointed in both directions.

The key lesson is simple. When a story depends on "profitable at scale," focus on whether revenue, absolute earnings, and net margin all move together in the reported numbers, particularly once regulators begin to push back.

What Airbnb's Recent Run Already Prices In

Airbnb shares now trade at US$181 after gaining 49.5% over the past year, and the bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St sees its Fair Value as sitting below that level.

The Narrative leans on strong execution but argues much of the optimistic booking, margin, and AI story is already priced in. For today's valuation to hold, a buyer would need to assume Airbnb's AI rebuild and new services keep offsetting regulatory and platform disintermediation pressure without eroding profitability.
